"""

IST 652 - Scripting for Data Analysis¶

Airbnb Price Analysis and Prediction - U.S. Markets¶

This program analyzes merged Airbnb data from 2020 and 2023, along with Consumer Price Index (CPI) data in JSON format, to address four key research questions:

  1. Price forecasting, for future Airbnb prices across key markets.
  2. Summary analysis of pricing patterns across different property characteristics with economic indicators.
  3. Categorical analysis of listings by temporal periods and geographic regions.
  4. Comparative analysis between different market segments and time periods.

Author: Brian Lee, Robin Nightingale, Hector Pena, Natajah Roberts

Data Source: Airbnb listings data (2020 & 2023) merged with Federal Reserve CPI data """

# state listing totals by room types chart
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Set style for better visuals
plt.style.use('default')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Chart: Top States Focus Chart
def create_top_states_chart():
    # Get top 10 states by total listings
    state_totals = airbnb_df['State'].value_counts().head(10)
    top_states = state_totals.index.tolist()

    # Filter data for top states
    filtered_df = airbnb_df[airbnb_df['State'].isin(top_states)]
    grouped_data = filtered_df.groupby(['State','room_type']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

    # Reorder by Entire home/apt count (decreasing)
    grouped_data = grouped_data.sort_values('Entire home/apt', ascending=False)

    plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
    ax = grouped_data.plot(kind='bar', ax=plt.gca(),
                          color=['#ff6b6b', '#4ecdc4', '#45b7d1'],
                          alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)

    # Add value labels on bars
    for container in ax.containers:
        ax.bar_label(container, fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

    plt.xlabel('State')
    plt.ylabel('Number of Listings')
    plt.title('Room Type Distribution - Top 10 States by Listing Volume',
              fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
    plt.legend(title='Room Type', frameon=True, fancybox=True, shadow=True)
    plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Run the visualizations
print("\n4. Top States Focus Chart")
create_top_states_chart()

# Summary statistics
print("\n" + "="*50)
print("DATA SUMMARY")
print("="*50)
print(f"Total listings: {len(airbnb_df):,}")
print(f"Number of states: {airbnb_df['State'].nunique()}")
print(f"Number of room types: {airbnb_df['room_type'].nunique()}")
print(f"Room types available: {', '.join(airbnb_df['room_type'].unique())}")
print(f"Top 3 states by volume: {', '.join(airbnb_df['State'].value_counts().head(3).index)}")

4. Top States Focus Chart

==================================================
DATA SUMMARY
==================================================
Total listings: 225,457
Number of states: 17
Number of room types: 4
Room types available: Private room, Entire home/apt, Hotel room, Shared room
Top 3 states by volume: California, New York, Florida

The top 10 states account for 187,786 Airbnb listings, with California dominating at 51,273 properties followed by New York's 37,366. Entire homes make up three-quarters of all listings, while private rooms represent most of the remainder. California and New York show more balanced property mixes, but southern states like Florida and Texas lean heavily toward entire home rentals. The concentration is striking - just three states control over half the market, and nearly every region favors whole-property rentals over shared accommodations.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Calculate average price by state
avg_price_by_state = airbnb_df.groupby('State')['price'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)

# Create the chart
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
bars = plt.bar(avg_price_by_state.index, avg_price_by_state.values,
               color='#ff6b6b', alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)

# Add value labels on top of bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    plt.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + max(avg_price_by_state) * 0.01,
             f'${height:.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

plt.xlabel('State')
plt.ylabel('Average Price ($)')
plt.title('Average Airbnb Price by State', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Print summary statistics
print("Average Price by State (Highest to Lowest):")
print("-" * 40)
for state, price in avg_price_by_state.items():
    print(f"{state:<15} ${price:.2f}")

print(f"\nHighest: {avg_price_by_state.index[0]} (${avg_price_by_state.iloc[0]:.2f})")
print(f"Lowest:  {avg_price_by_state.index[-1]} (${avg_price_by_state.iloc[-1]:.2f})")
print(f"Overall Average: ${airbnb_df['price'].mean():.2f}")

Texas leads with the highest average Airbnb prices at $287.50, followed by Pennsylvania ($247.06) and Florida ($228.34). Mid-tier states like California ($204.29) and Nevada ($200.60) cluster around $200, while major markets New York ($150.36) and Washington D.C. ($150.65) surprisingly rank in the lower half. Maine has the lowest average prices at $126.22, with a $161 spread between the highest and lowest state averages.

avg_price_data = airbnb_df.groupby(['State', 'room_type'])['price'].mean().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Sort states by Hotel room average price (descending)
hotel_room_avg_price = airbnb_df[airbnb_df['room_type'] == 'Hotel room'].groupby('State')['price'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
avg_price_data = avg_price_data.reindex(hotel_room_avg_price.index)

# Create the chart
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
ax = avg_price_data.plot(kind='bar', ax=plt.gca(),
                        color=['#ff6b6b', '#4ecdc4', '#45b7d1', '#f9ca24'],
                        alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)

# Add value labels on bars
for container in ax.containers:
    ax.bar_label(container, fmt='$%.0f', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

plt.xlabel('State')
plt.ylabel('Average Price ($)')
plt.title('Average Airbnb Price by State and Room Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(title='Room Type', frameon=True, fancybox=True, shadow=True)
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Texas leads in pricing across most categories, with entire homes averaging $322 and even shared rooms hitting $121. Pennsylvania and Florida follow with high entire home rates around $250-270, though Pennsylvania shows extreme hotel room pricing at $537. Most states price entire homes between $160-250, while private rooms cluster around $80-100 across regions. Shared rooms stay under $80 everywhere except Texas and Maine, with Maine being an outlier at $155. Hotel rooms vary wildly from $94 in Washington D.C. to over $600 in Florida, suggesting different market dynamics. The data reveals Texas as the premium market, while states like Washington and Illinois offer more affordable entire home options under $170.

# Create monthly price averages using the correct date column

    monthly_prices = airbnb_df.groupby('Year-Month')['price'].mean().reset_index()
    monthly_prices['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(monthly_prices['Year-Month'] + '-01')
elif 'last_review' in airbnb_df.columns:
    # Use last_review column to create Year-Month
    airbnb_df['Year-Month'] = airbnb_df['last_review'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
    monthly_prices = airbnb_df.groupby('Year-Month')['price'].mean().reset_index()
    monthly_prices['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(monthly_prices['Year-Month'] + '-01')
else:
    # Fallback: use Year column if available
    if 'Year' in airbnb_df.columns:
        yearly_prices = airbnb_df.groupby('Year')['price'].mean().reset_index()
        yearly_prices['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(yearly_prices['Year'].astype(str) + '-01-01')
        monthly_prices = yearly_prices.rename(columns={'Year': 'Year-Month'})
        monthly_prices['Year-Month'] = monthly_prices['Date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
    else:
        print("No suitable date column found. Cannot create time series chart.")
        monthly_prices = pd.DataFrame()

if not monthly_prices.empty:
    monthly_prices = monthly_prices.sort_values('Date')

    print("Monthly prices data:")

    # Merge with CPI data
    monthly_comparison = pd.merge(monthly_prices, cpi_df[['Year-Month', 'CPI_Value']], on='Year-Month', how='inner')

    print(f"Monthly comparison data shape: {monthly_comparison.shape}")
    print("Monthly comparison sample:")

    # Check if we have data to plot

        print("No matching data found between Airbnb and CPI datasets")

        # Dual axis plot

        # Plot price on left axis

        ax1.set_xlabel('Date', fontweight='bold')
        ax1.set_ylabel('Average Airbnb Price ($)', color=color1, fontweight='bold')
        line1 = ax1.plot(monthly_comparison['Date'], monthly_comparison['price'],
                        color=color1, linewidth=3, marker='o', markersize=4, label='Airbnb Price')

        # Add trend line for Airbnb prices
        x_numeric = np.arange(len(monthly_comparison))
        z = np.polyfit(x_numeric, monthly_comparison['price'], 1)
        p = np.poly1d(z)
        trend_line = ax1.plot(monthly_comparison['Date'], p(x_numeric),
                             color='darkblue', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.8,
                             label=f'Price Trend (slope: ${z[0]:.2f}/month)')

        ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color1)
        ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

        # Plot CPI on right axis
        ax2 = ax1.twinx()
        color2 = 'tab:red'
        ax2.set_ylabel('Consumer Price Index (CPI)', color=color2, fontweight='bold')
        line2 = ax2.plot(monthly_comparison['Date'], monthly_comparison['CPI_Value'],
                        color=color2, linewidth=3, marker='s', markersize=4, label='CPI')

        # Add trend line for CPI
        z_cpi = np.polyfit(x_numeric, monthly_comparison['CPI_Value'], 1)
        p_cpi = np.poly1d(z_cpi)
        trend_line_cpi = ax2.plot(monthly_comparison['Date'], p_cpi(x_numeric),
                                 color='darkred', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.8,
                                 label=f'CPI Trend (slope: {z_cpi[0]:.2f}/month)')

        ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color2)

        # Add title and legend
        plt.title('Airbnb Prices vs Consumer Price Index Over Time (with Trend Lines)',
                 fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)

        # Combine all lines for legend
        lines = line1 + trend_line + line2 + trend_line_cpi
        labels = [l.get_label() for l in lines]
        ax1.legend(lines, labels, loc='upper left', frameon=True, fancybox=True, shadow=True)

        # Add correlation coefficient text
        correlation = np.corrcoef(monthly_comparison['price'], monthly_comparison['CPI_Value'])[0, 1]
        ax1.text(0.02, 0.98, f'Correlation: {correlation:.3f}',
                transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor='lightgray', alpha=0.8),
                verticalalignment='top')

        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
else:
    print("Cannot create time series chart - no valid date data found")

"""## 2. DATA PREPROCESSING FOR MODELING

"""
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error, r2_score

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("DATA PREPROCESSING FOR MODELING")
print("="*60)

# Convert last_review to datetime and create time-based features
# Check if 'last_review' is already datetime, if not, convert
if not pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(airbnb_df['last_review']):
    airbnb_df['last_review'] = pd.to_datetime(airbnb_df['last_review'], errors='coerce')

# Create Year-Month column from last_review, handling potential NaT values
airbnb_df['Year-Month'] = airbnb_df['last_review'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')

# Merge with CPI data. Use how='left' to keep all airbnb data, even if no CPI match
print("Merging Airbnb data with CPI...")
# Ensure cpi_df has 'Year-Month' in the correct format for merging
cpi_df['Year-Month'] = cpi_df['Date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')

# Perform the merge, using suffixes to handle duplicate column names if any
airbnb_merged = pd.merge(airbnb_df, cpi_df[['Year-Month', 'CPI_Value']], on='Year-Month', how='left', suffixes=('_airbnb', '_cpi'))
print(f"Merged dataset shape: {airbnb_merged.shape}")

# Handle missing values
print("\nHandling missing values...")
missing_before = airbnb_merged.isnull().sum()
print("Missing values before cleaning:")
print(missing_before[missing_before > 0])

# Filll missing CPI values with interpolation. Use the correct CPI column name from the merge.
cpi_col_name = None
if 'CPI_Value_cpi' in airbnb_merged.columns:
    cpi_col_name = 'CPI_Value_cpi'
elif 'CPI_Value' in airbnb_merged.columns:
     cpi_col_name = 'CPI_Value'

if cpi_col_name:
    airbnb_merged[cpi_col_name] = airbnb_merged[cpi_col_name].fillna(method='ffill').fillna(method='bfill')
    print(f"Filled missing values in '{cpi_col_name}'")
else:
    print("CPI column not found in merged dataframe. Cannot fill missing CPI values.")


# Handle missing reviews data
airbnb_merged['reviews_per_month'] = airbnb_merged['reviews_per_month'].fillna(0)
airbnb_merged['last_review'] = airbnb_merged['last_review'].fillna(airbnb_merged['last_review'].median())
# Fill missing host_name values
airbnb_merged['host_name'] = airbnb_merged['host_name'].fillna('Unknown')


# Remove outliers (prices beyond reasonable range)
Q1 = airbnb_merged['price'].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = airbnb_merged['price'].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
# A more robust way to define bounds, allowing for some high prices but excluding extremes
# Using a multiplier like 3 or 5 for upper bound might be better depending on distribution
lower_bound = airbnb_merged['price'].quantile(0.01) # Use 1st percentile as lower bound
upper_bound = airbnb_merged['price'].quantile(0.99) # Use 99th percentile as upper bound


print(f"Price outlier bounds (1st-99th percentile): ${lower_bound:.2f} - ${upper_bound:.2f}")
# Filter based on the new bounds
airbnb_clean = airbnb_merged[(airbnb_merged['price'] >= lower_bound) & (airbnb_merged['price'] <= upper_bound)].copy() # Use .copy() to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning


outliers_removed_count = len(airbnb_merged) - len(airbnb_clean)
print(f"Outliers removed: {outliers_removed_count:,} listings")
print(f"Clean dataset shape: {airbnb_clean.shape}")

# feature Engineering
print("\nFeature Engineering...")

# categorical encoding
le = LabelEncoder()
# Include 'neighborhood_group' and 'neighborhood' as they might be useful
categorical_features = ['City', 'State', 'room_type', 'neighborhood_group', 'neighborhood']

for feature in categorical_features:
    if feature in airbnb_clean.columns:
        # Handle potential NaN values in categorical columns before encoding
        airbnb_clean[f'{feature}_encoded'] = le.fit_transform(airbnb_clean[feature].astype(str).fillna('Missing'))
    else:
        print(f"Warning: Categorical feature '{feature}' not found in airbnb_clean.")


# Create additional features
#airbnb_clean['price_per_review'] = airbnb_clean['price'] / (airbnb_clean['number_of_reviews'] + 1)
airbnb_clean['reviews_density'] = airbnb_clean['reviews_per_month'] * 12  # Annual reviews estimate

# Interaction feature: Price * CPI (if CPI column exists)
# if cpi_col_name and cpi_col_name in airbnb_clean.columns:

    try:
        decomposition = seasonal_decompose(monthly_data['price'], model='additive', period=12)

        # Plot decomposition
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(15, 12))
        decomposition.observed.plot(ax=axes[0], title='Observed Price', color='blue')
        decomposition.trend.plot(ax=axes[1], title='Trend', color='green')
        decomposition.seasonal.plot(ax=axes[2], title='Seasonal', color='orange')
        decomposition.resid.plot(ax=axes[3], title='Residual', color='red')

        plt.suptitle('Seasonal Decomposition of Airbnb Prices', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Seasonal decomposition failed: {e}")

cpi_series = cpi_series.iloc[:min_length]

# Generate forecasts for 2024-2027
print("\nGenerating price forecasts for 2024-2027...")

# Only generate forecasts if a model was successfully fitted
if model_fitted:
    # Create future CPI values (assuming historical growth rate)
    cpi_growth_rate = (cpi_series.iloc[-1] / cpi_series.iloc[0]) ** (1/len(cpi_series)) - 1
    print(f"Historical CPI growth rate: {cpi_growth_rate:.4f}")

    # Generate future dates and CPI values
    future_periods = 48  # 4 years * 12 months
    last_date = monthly_data.index[-1]
    future_dates = pd.date_range(start=last_date + pd.DateOffset(months=1), periods=future_periods, freq='MS')
    future_cpi = [cpi_series.iloc[-1] * (1 + cpi_growth_rate) ** i for i in range(1, future_periods + 1)]

    # Generate forecasts based on model type
    try:
        if PMDARIMA_AVAILABLE and hasattr(model_fitted, 'predict'):
            # pmdarima auto_arima model
            forecast = model_fitted.predict(n_periods=future_periods, exogenous=future_cpi)
            forecast_result = model_fitted.predict(n_periods=future_periods, exogenous=future_cpi, return_conf_int=True)
            if isinstance(forecast_result, tuple):
                forecast = forecast_result[0]
                forecast_ci = forecast_result[1]
            else:
                forecast = forecast_result
                # Create simple confidence intervals
                forecast_std = np.std(price_series) * 0.1
                forecast_ci = np.column_stack([forecast - 1.96*forecast_std, forecast + 1.96*forecast_std])
        else:
            # statsmodels ARIMA model
            forecast_result = model_fitted.forecast(steps=future_periods, exog=future_cpi)
            if hasattr(forecast_result, 'conf_int'):
                forecast = forecast_result.predicted_mean
                forecast_ci = forecast_result.conf_int().values
            else:
                forecast = forecast_result
                # Create simple confidence intervals
                forecast_std = np.std(price_series) * 0.1
                forecast_ci = np.column_stack([forecast - 1.96*forecast_std, forecast + 1.96*forecast_std])

        # Create forecast dataframe
        forecast_df = pd.DataFrame({
            'Date': future_dates,
            'Forecast': forecast,
            'Lower_CI': forecast_ci[:, 0],
            'Upper_CI': forecast_ci[:, 1],
            'CPI_Forecast': future_cpi
        })

        print("Price forecast sample (2024-2025):")
        print(forecast_df.head(24))

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Forecast generation failed: {e}")
        print("Creating simplified forecast based on trend...")

        # Simple trend-based forecast as fallback
        recent_trend = np.polyfit(range(len(price_series)), price_series, 1)[0]
        last_price = price_series.iloc[-1]

        simple_forecast = [last_price + recent_trend * i for i in range(1, future_periods + 1)]
        forecast_std = np.std(price_series) * 0.1

        forecast_df = pd.DataFrame({
            'Date': future_dates,
            'Forecast': simple_forecast,
            'Lower_CI': [f - 1.96*forecast_std for f in simple_forecast],
            'Upper_CI': [f + 1.96*forecast_std for f in simple_forecast],
            'CPI_Forecast': future_cpi
        })

        print("Simple trend-based forecast generated")

else:
    print("ARIMA model fitting failed, cannot generate forecast.")
    # Create an empty forecast_df to avoid errors in subsequent cells
    forecast_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=['Date', 'Forecast', 'Lower_CI', 'Upper_CI', 'CPI_Forecast'])

### Multiple Algorithm Comparison for Cross-Validation
"""

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("MACHINE LEARNING PRICE PREDICTION")
print("="*60)

# Prepare features for ML models
# FIXED:
feature_columns = [
    'latitude', 'longitude', 'minimum_nights', 'number_of_reviews',
    'reviews_per_month', 'calculated_host_listings_count', 'CPI_Value',
    'City_encoded', 'State_encoded', 'room_type_encoded', 'neighborhood_encoded',
    'reviews_density', 'host_experience_encoded', 'days_since_last_review',
    'month', 'quarter', 'review_activity_score'
]
# Select features that exist in the dataset
available_features = [col for col in feature_columns if col in airbnb_clean.columns]
print(f"Available features for modeling: {available_features}")

X = airbnb_clean[available_features].fillna(0)
y = airbnb_clean['price']

# Feature scaling
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
X_scaled = pd.DataFrame(X_scaled, columns=available_features)

# Train-test split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_scaled, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Import ML models
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeRegressor
from sklearn.svm import SVR

# Define models
models = {
    'Linear Regression': LinearRegression(),
    'Ridge Regression': Ridge(alpha=1.0),
    'Lasso Regression': Lasso(alpha=1.0),
    'Decision Tree': DecisionTreeRegressor(random_state=42),
    'Random Forest': RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42),
    'Gradient Boosting': GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42),
    'SVR': SVR(kernel='rbf')
}

# Model evaluation
results = {}
print("Model Performance Comparison:")
print("-" * 60)

for name, model in models.items():
    # Train model
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)

    # Make predictions
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

    # Calculate metrics
    mse = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mse)
    mae = mean_absolute_error(y_test, y_pred)
    r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_pred)

    results[name] = {'R²': r2, 'RMSE': rmse, 'MAE': mae}

    print(f"{name:<18} R²: {r2:.4f}  RMSE: ${rmse:.2f}  MAE: ${mae:.2f}")

Model Performance Summary: Random Forest achieved the best results with 37.6% variance explained (R² = 0.376) and lowest prediction error ($113 RMSE). Gradient Boosting ranked second at 24.6% variance explained ($125 RMSE). Linear regression models (Linear, Ridge, Lasso) performed identically at 15.7% variance explained with $132 RMSE. Decision Tree failed completely with negative R² (-0.269) and highest error ($162 RMSE). SVR showed the weakest performance among functional models at 12.8% variance explained ($134 RMSE).

Feature Importance Summary: Geographic location drives Airbnb pricing more than any other factor. Latitude and longitude combined account for 31% of the Random Forest model's predictive power (15.8% each), showing that precise positioning within markets significantly affects prices. Room type ranks third at 11.9% importance, confirming that entire homes versus private rooms remains a key pricing factor. The gap between location and property type suggests micro-location matters more than broad categories. Review metrics show moderate influence rather than dominance. Recent activity (days since last review at 7.6% and review activity score at 7.6%) outweighs total review volume (5.3%), indicating that current guest engagement affects pricing more than historical performance. Host portfolio size contributes 6.5% importance while neighborhood identity adds 5.9%, showing that management scale and hyperlocal factors matter but remain secondary to broader geographic positioning. No single factor dominates pricing decisions - the top feature explains less than 16% of model behavior. This balanced distribution across location, property type, and engagement metrics helps explain why overall prediction accuracy remains modest at 37.6%.
